records.reachability_note: every budget estimate encodes through this table.

exercised.note: 36 golden cases regenerated from the `ai-tokenizer` oracle pass, and a token-count estimate is checked against them.

records.guarantee: `encode_ordinary` produces the same token ids as `ai-tokenizer`'s claude encoding for every golden case, and `estimate_tokens` returns their count.
records.fault_timing: A vocabulary or pre-tokenizer divergence that keeps counts equal but changes ids.
records.required_faults: The golden corpus, produced by the oracle and not by the crate.

confidence.evidence: [evidence](evidence/tokenizer-encoding-matches-the-independent-oracle.md). The corpus texts that named the predecessor were replaced at U3 and the golden regenerated once with `gen/gen-token-golden.ts` against the oracle.

records.impact: Budget fitting over- or under-counts and a session overflows or truncates the context window.

records.reachability_note: the vocabulary is read at build time.

exercised.note: the generator rejects duplicate ranks and requires all 256 single bytes; no Rust test asserts the embedded asset's completeness.

records.guarantee: The embedded `claude.tiktoken` asset has unique ranks and covers every single byte, so every input encodes without a fallback.

check.condition: ranks are unique and 256 single-byte tokens exist in the asset.

records.fault_timing: A truncated or duplicated asset makes some bytes unencodable.

confidence.evidence: [evidence](evidence/tokenizer-vocabulary-is-embedded-and-complete.md). `gen/gen-claude-vocab.ts` enforces both conditions when it writes the asset; the Rust side trusts the asset.

records.existing_check: The generator's checks; no Rust check; unaudited.
records.impact: Encoding panics or silently drops bytes.
